name: Name

roleHints.admin: Manages everything: members, API keys, settings
roleHints.member: Creates and edits data, workflows and pages
roleHints.end_user: Only opens the pages meant for them

versions.title: Version history
versions.description: Every save creates a version. Restoring puts an older version back online, without deleting anything.

secretPicker.newDescription: The value is encrypted and never shown again, not even to your AI. Only its name is kept here.
secretPicker.missing: The credential {name} does not exist in this workspace.

claude.codeLogin: Then type /mcp in Claude Code and sign in.
claude.desktop: Claude Desktop or claude.ai: Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector, paste the link above.

chatgpt.steps: On chatgpt.com/plugins, click "+" then "Add custom MCP server". Paste the link above, pick OAuth, accept the warning and click "Create as a plugin". In a chat, type @ to use it.
chatgpt.note: Web only. Business and Enterprise/Edu plans can read and change data; Pro can only read.

gemini.cliLogin: Then type /mcp auth runbase to sign in.
gemini.web: Gemini app: gemini.google.com > Settings > Connected Apps > Add a custom app, paste the link above (availability limited).

cursor.login: Cursor asks you to sign in the first time you use it.

codex.steps: Run these two commands to add Runbase and sign in.

other.oauth: Any AI agent that supports MCP: paste the link above. It signs in with OAuth.
other.key: Tools without sign-in (scripts, CI): send an API key in this header.

adminOnly: Only an administrator can change this.

workflows.p1: Every morning at 9am, send me on Slack the leads created yesterday with a score above 70
workflows.p2: When a Typeform is submitted, create the lead and notify #sales
workflows.p3: When a deal moves to Won, create the customer and send a welcome email

functions.p1: Add a function that scores a lead from its company domain
functions.p2: Add a function that cleans up phone numbers to international format
functions.p3: Add a function that finds the company name from an email address

events.p1: Send a “lead.qualified” event when a lead's score goes above 70
events.p2: When a “payment.received” event arrives, mark the deal as paid

webhooks.p1: Create a webhook for Stripe payments and log each payment on the matching company
webhooks.p2: When a Typeform is submitted, create the lead and notify #sales
webhooks.p3: Create a webhook for Cal.com bookings that adds the meeting to the contact

pages.p1: Create a page to track my leads by status, with a form to add one
pages.p2: Create a pipeline page showing open deals by stage and their total amount

queries.p1: Save a query for revenue won per month
queries.p2: Save a query counting new leads per source this week

databases.p1: Create a CRM with Contacts, Companies and Deals tables, linked together
databases.p2: Create a Leads table with name, email, company, source and score
databases.p3: Import my HubSpot contacts into a Contacts table

records.p1: Import this CSV of leads into this table, without duplicates on email
records.p2: Add 5 realistic sample records so I can test my workflows
records.p3: Create a workflow that fills the company of each new record from its email

runs.p1: Run my lead scoring workflow on the 10 latest leads
runs.p2: Every Monday at 8am, send me on Slack a summary of last week's deals

approvals.p1: Before sending an outreach email, ask for my approval
approvals.p2: When a deal above 10k is marked Won, wait for my approval before invoicing

errors.p1: Check my workflows and tell me which ones could fail
errors.p2: If a workflow fails, notify me on Slack with the reason

credentials.p1: Which credentials do my workflows need? Tell me which ones are missing
credentials.p2: Set up the HubSpot sync: tell me which key to add here
